thread:
maria: heads up — after the quick header-rewrite push the /v1/generate route started returning 502s for a subset of requests. I flipped the emergency rewrite toggle in the console to short-circuit to passthrough, but traffic still shows spikes.

aj: which toggle exactly? link? :eyes:

maria: Console > Routing > route-id=generate-v1 > Overrides > header_rewrite. I set it from "x-accept: internal" back to "none" at 17:01, but the upstream still rejects a percent of requests (502).

kevin: can you paste the exact header that was being injected? I want to grep the proxy logs.

maria: it was this: `x-redwood-client: internal-v2` we added a path-specific rewrite, thought it was safe.

linh: deploy-bot shows the toggle action succeeded: `deploy-bot: route override header_rewrite removed by maria at 17:01` — but TTL on some gateway caches is 60s and there are active long-polling clients. We might have stale route entries.

aj: ok can we force an immediate config reload on the edge nodes? If we can trigger reload, that should clear the stale header map.

kevin: running curl against /admin/reload on a few nodes worked for me:```\nkevin: for n in edge-1 edge-2 edge-3; do ssh infra@$n 'curl -sS -XPOST http://127.0.0.1:9001/reload'; done\nkevin: ```

linh: did that. metrics show error-rate falling on edge-2 and edge-3, edge-1 still high. Investigating.

maria: aj can you hold the circuit-breaker at 70% success to limit backend overload? I don't want a full traffic cut.

aj: setting CB to 70% now. console: Routing > generate-v1 > Circuit-breaker > success_threshold=0.7. Done.

oncall-bot: incident-mode: partial-mitigation applied by aj. Incident ID INC-2024-211.

kevin: found a bad config in the egress mapping for region ap-east that rewrites downstream host header incorrectly when x-redwood-client present. That explains why only some upstream shards failed. Pushing a scoped hotfix to only ap-east to stop rewrite.

maria: thanks. after kevin's scoped patch + edge reload, errors dropped to baseline. Are we doing a full rollback of the original feature (header-rewrite) or re-deploy with safe guards?

linh: I'd vote to keep the header-rewrite disabled globally until we run a canary that includes the ap-east fix, and add a config lint to prevent host-rewrite + client-header combos.

aj: +1. I'll update the rollout policy in the console to require region-gated canary for header rewrites. Also adding a preflight check: verify egress-mapping no-op for unknown x-redwood-client values.

maria: action list: 1) keep header_rewrite toggle OFF globally (done), 2) add lint to CI to catch host+client rewrite combos (kevin), 3) run canary in us-west only for 30m (aj), 4) postmortem with timeline (maria).

kevin: filing PR for lint now -> #PR-4512.

maria: I'll take postmortem. tagging @oncall-bot to track followups. Thanks all — great containment. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: followup tasks created: INC-2024-211 -> tasks: [run-canary-us-west, ci-lint-pr, postmortem-draft].
